q: An electron moves from a point whose potential is $20\,\text{V}$ to a point whose potential is $70\,\text{V}$. Does its potential energy increase or decrease, and by how much in electronvolts?
a: The potential energy of the electron is $-eV$, so it decreases when the potential increases: the change is $-e \cdot (70\,\text{V} - 20\,\text{V}) = -50\,\text{eV}$.
